body:
I think that almost nobody is going to use `$all` because if we still have the line break in there it will mess up peoples custom prompts. For example:
```toml
# Use custom format
format = """
[┌───────────────────>](bold green)
[│](bold green)$directory$rust$package
[└─>](bold green) """
```
Replacing the `$directory$rust$package` with `$all` would completely mess up the prompt and while you can hide something like the `character` module by clearing it's format you can't easily just hide the `line_break`.

Or a second option would be just removing `$all` outright and just setting the default to something like this (based on the current default):
```toml
format = """

$username\
$hostname\
$kubernetes\
$directory\
$git_branch\
$git_commit\
$git_state\
$git_status\
$hg_branch\
$docker_context\
$package\
$dotnet\
$elixir\
$elm\
$erlang\
$golang\
$haskell\
$java\
$julia\
$nim\
$nodejs\
$ocaml\
$php\
$purescript\
$python\
$ruby\
$rust\
$terraform\
$zig\
$nix_shell\
$conda\
$memory_usage\
$aws\
$env_var\
$crystal\
$cmd_duration\
$custom\
\n
$jobs\
$battery\
$time\
$character
"""
```

Then people could easily copy this remove the `\n` and build the custom format around that.

+#### Conditional Format Strings
+
+A conditional format string wrapped in `(` and `)` will not render if all variables inside are empty.
+
+For example:
+
+- `(@$region)` will show nothing if the variable `region` is `None`, otherwise `@` followed by the value of region.
+- `(some text)` will always show nothing since there are no variables wrapped in the braces.
+- When `$all` is a shortcut for `\[$a$b\] `, `($all)` will show nothing only if `$a` and `$b` are both `None`.
+  This works the same as `(\[$a$b\] )`.
+
+#### Escapable characters
+
+The following symbols have special usage in a format string.
+If you want to print the following symbols, you have to escape them with a backslash (`\`).
+
+- $
+- \\
+- [
+- ]
+- (
+- )
+
+Note that `toml` has [its own escape syntax](https://github.com/toml-lang/toml#user-content-string).
+It is recommended to use a literal string (`''`) in your config.
+If you want to use a basic string (`""`), pay attention to escape the backslash `\`.
+
+For example, when you want to print a `$` symbol on a new line, the following configs for `format` are equivalent:
+
+```toml
+# with basic string
+format = "\n\\$"
+
+# with multiline basic string
+format = """
+
+\\$"""
+
+# with literal string

+
+\$'''
